description:
EDA (Energiewirtschaftliches Datenaustausch) integration for Energy Community
v2 tenants (EnergyCommunity 4.6+ and Basic.Energy 1.7+, stream-data storage for
metering values — ADR 0001, AB#4550).

Installs:
- EDA adapter (System.Communication/Adapter) — deployed via Communication Operator,
  AdapterConfiguration skeleton with empty credentials (fill in Refinery Studio before deploy)
- 15 EDA pipelines in 8 DataFlows: receive-eda-messages, handle-daten-crmsg,
  request-all-metering-points, request-consumption-reports,
  request-missing-consumption-reports, energy-set-states-depending-on-meteringpoints
  each keep their own DataFlow; start-eda-process carries two (the HTTP endpoint
  and `Start planned EDA processes`, 2.2.1); the seven process-message handlers (EC_REQ_ONL,
  EC_PODLIST, EC_PRTFACT_CHANGE, CR_REQ_PT, CM_REV_SP, CM_REV_CUS, CM_REV_IMP)
  share the DataFlow `eda-handle-process-messages` (6a3ba517dd34215646b7a8a4,
  AB#4820) and carry their process name on the Pipeline itself. All seven run
  on FromPolling@1 with staggered intervals (2:05 / 2:55 / 3:10 / 3:35 / 4:20 /
  5:00 / 5:40) so they never poll the EDA adapter in lockstep;
  FromExecutePipelineCommand@1 stays in each definition, commented out, as the
  manual fallback. receive-eda-messages (1:05) and handle-daten-crmsg (0:42) poll
  as well since 2.6.0, each in its own DataFlow: deploying the DataFlow switches
  reception or the stream-data ingest on, undeploying it switches it off.
  `Start planned EDA processes` polls every 10 minutes
- 2 System.Communication/PipelineTrigger: `request-all-metering-points`
  (69e1b8a1870f4f0d6e91e630) fires its pipeline daily at 04:00 via cron
  (`0 0 4 * * *`) instead of an explicit ExecutePipelineCommand — ported from
  the energy-community-deployment reference, hence the new System.Bot
  dependency (System.Bot/CronExpression). `request-low-quality-data`
  (69dde3c2870f4f0d6e91e61e) fires request-consumption-reports daily at 05:00
  (`0 0 5 * * *`, 2.7.0), as the 1.x tenants ran it
- `Start planned EDA processes` (6a2bc26a6830b2865f042892) starts EdaProcess
  entities flagged Planned once their StartTime is due; Sender/Receiver are
  already set by the HTTP pipeline when the process is created, so the update
  step leaves them untouched (ported from energy-community-deployment, 2.2.1)
- 16 EDA-internal queries (process tracking, metering-point lookups,
  participation periods, planned processes)
- EDA cockpit MeshBoard (System.UI/Dashboard `energy-community-eda` +
  widgets, AB#4578): metering-point count KPI, state donut, and two
  EdaProcess tables (errored: success==false / open: finished==false) over a
  new SimpleRtQuery on Basic.Energy/EdaProcess. Requires the service-managed
  System.UI CK model (octo-platform-services running).

EC v2 changes vs. the 1.x line:
- handle-daten-crmsg writes 15-minute stream data: ParseConsumptionRecord@1 ->
  Basic.Energy/EnergyMeasurement anchor entities (well-known name
  <meteringPointRtId>_<obisCode>, deduped via UpdateRtEntityIfNewer@1) ->
  SaveTimeRangeStreamDataInArchive@1 into the Base 2.x raw archive
  energy-measurements (ec0000000000000000000a01). No more per-interval
  EnergyQuantity entities and no overlap delete/insert reconciliation.
- All pipelines and queries use the v2 types directly: Basic.Energy/EdaMessage,
  EdaProcess, EdaMeteringPoint, MeteringPoint, OperatingFacility and the
  Basic.Energy/MessageToProcess association. EnergyCommunity/Consumer,
  Producer, Customer and ParticipationPeriod remain EnergyCommunity types.
- request-consumption-reports and request-missing-consumption-reports find
  their days in the stream data (2.7.0, AB#4551): the 1.x line read them from
  the daily EnergyCommunity/EnergyQuantity entities, which no longer exist.
  Days with L3 values come from the daily rollup energy-measurements-daily
  (ec0000000000000000000a03), metering points without a value on a day from
  the raw archive (ec0000000000000000000a01).

Prerequisites:
- EnergyCommunity.Base 2.x installed (provides the energy-measurements
  stream-data archives; activate them before deploying the EDA data flows —
  the raw archive and the roll-up ladder up to energy-measurements-daily,
  which request-consumption-reports reads)

Post-install:
- Fill AdapterConfiguration JSON (EdaHttpAdapter.Host, User, Password, IsSimulationMode)
  on the EDA adapter entity in Refinery Studio
- octo-cli -c DeployWorkload -id 686e0f17196fcd3c42ed8c77   # EDA adapter
- The cron triggers of request-all-metering-points and
  request-consumption-reports ship DeploymentState 0 like every other EDA
  entity and go live with the DeployDataFlow of their DataFlow
  (DeployTriggers deploys all triggers of a tenant at once). From then on
  request-consumption-reports sends CR_REQ_PT requests every morning
- DeployDataFlow per DataFlow — pipelines are pre-assigned to the EDA adapter
  via Executes-1, no manual assignment needed. One call covers all seven
  process handlers:
  octo-cli -c DeployDataFlow --identifier 6a3ba517dd34215646b7a8a4
- Deploying receive-eda-messages (68b01ae68f03da854927fd9e) starts fetching from
  the market communication within the first poll. Deploy it last, with the
  adapter configuration in place

Upgrading a tenant from 2.1.x (AB#4820):
- The seven per-handler DataFlows were removed from the seed. Removing them
  from the seed does NOT delete them on an installed tenant — run
  `UndeployDataFlow` on each, then
  `octo-cli -c UpdateBlueprint -tv EnergyCommunity.EdaIntegration-2.2.0 -m Full`
  (preview it first — the delete is a permanent Erase). See README.md.

2.4.0 splits the seed across one file per topic (AB#4758 `seedDataPaths`) —
identical entities, no data change. It therefore requires an engine that knows
`seedDataPaths`: an older engine drops the unknown property, finds no
`seedDataPath` and installs an EMPTY seed while still reporting success.
Install 2.3.1 on such tenants.

2.4.1 fixes the `EC_PODLIST` handler: its `Eda metering points` If@1 step
tested `$.Consumer.Rows[0].RtId` instead of `$.EdaMeteringPoint.Rows[0].RtId`,
so it branched on the wrong query result. Pipeline definition only — no
entity added, removed or re-parented.

2.4.1 -> 2.5.0: handle-daten-crmsg writes its slots through the new
SaveTimeRangeSeriesInArchive@1 instead of a nested ForEach that built one
runtime entity per 15-minute window. The old shape ran CreateUpdateInfo@1 +
CreateAssociationUpdate@1 per slot, flattened the result twice with JSONPath
wildcards, filtered the candidates through UpdateRtEntityIfNewer@1 and wrote
them with a separate ApplyChanges@2 — roughly two dozen node executions and one
fully materialised entity per quarter hour, to produce one archive row with
four values. Measured on a full replay of a productive tenant: 316,268 rows in
4,530 s, i.e. 78 rows/second or 12.8 ms per slot, with the database nowhere
near the bottleneck. The runtime model only ever needs one anchor entity per
(metering point x OBIS code) — 16 of them on that tenant, built from 316,268
candidates.

The pipeline also maps the message's own DocumentCreationDateTime onto the
archive's SourceDocumentDate column and the reading's quality onto DataQuality.
Base 2.6.0 declares both as the archive's Archive.ConflictPrecedence keys, in
that order: a measurement is never displaced by an estimate, and within one
quality level the newer source document wins. The stored value therefore no
longer depends on the order messages arrive in — which is more than the 1.x line
guaranteed (FilterEnergyData@1 sorted by CreationTime and ranked quality
nowhere).

handle-daten-crmsg also loads 50 messages per run instead of 30. With the
archive written as multi-row statements a run costs ~33 ms per message plus a
fixed ~1 s, so fewer runs shorten a bulk replay (octogrid, 900 messages: 75 ms
per message at 30, 69 ms at 50). The ceiling is hard: GetRtEntitiesByType@1
returns the whole batch as ONE MongoDB document, capped at 16 MB, and a batch
over the cap fails every run without marking anything processed, so the pipeline
stalls on it for good. Message sizes are skewed — octogrid averages 55 KB, but its
largest four are 0.9 to 2.1 MB — so the bound is the sum of the `take` LARGEST
messages: 10.6 MB at 50, 14.6 MB at 100. scripts/migration/ec-v2/01-baseline.js
reports that worst case for a tenant; lower take where it exceeds ~12 MB.

Requires Base 2.6.0 (the archive columns and the precedence declaration, now also the
blueprint dependency floor) and an EDA adapter built with SaveTimeRangeSeriesInArchive@1
(octo-mesh-adapter, AB#5248) whose ParseConsumptionRecord@1 carries the document creation
time (octo-adapter-eda, AB#5249). An older parser leaves that time at 0001-01-01: the
quality key still decides, but two deliveries of equal quality fall back to arrival order.

2.5.0 -> 2.6.0: the pipelines behave like the 1.x pipelines the migrated communities ran.
The seed had been created from an older state of the 1.x deployment and never received
what the 1.x line changed afterwards:
- receive-eda-messages attaches a message to its process even when that process is already
  finished; the lookup no longer filters on Finished (1.x AB#3775).
- handle-daten-crmsg sends ONE ABLEHNUNG_CRMSG per original message for an unknown metering
  point. receive-eda-messages splits a DATEN_CRMSG covering more than a day and extends the
  MessageId of each part; the handler rejected every part, each with an id the sender does
  not know. It now cuts the id back to the original 35 characters, and only the first part
  answers (1.x AB#3774). The 1.x line collapsed the parts of one run; a message with more
  parts than a run loads was still rejected once per run.
- handle-cm-rev-cus and handle-cm-rev-imp write the reason of the revocation into the
  metering point's Description: "AUFHEBUNG_CCMC: Kunde ausgetreten" and
  "AUFHEBUNG_CCMI: <ResponseInfo>" (1.x AB#3776).
- handle-ec-req-onl reads producers and consumers through the queries pipeline_producer /
  pipeline_consumer again: CreateMeteringPointUpdate@1 takes the existing production type
  from the query row (1.x AB#3939). It also updates the process in three guarded steps, so
  that a ZUSTIMMUNG_ECON arriving after ABSCHLUSS_ECON no longer resets Finished or blanks
  the result (1.x AB#4036).
- `Start EDA process HTTP request` stores a request that carries a start date as a PLANNED
  process (Planned, StartTime = that date, ProcessData, ConversationId "-"). For such a
  request EdaStartProcess@1 creates and sends nothing; the pipeline stored it as a started
  process all the same, so a participation-factor change for a later day was neither sent
  nor planned. `Start planned EDA processes` sends it when it is due (1.x AB#3147).
- receive-eda-messages, handle-daten-crmsg and `Start planned EDA processes` ship with
  FromPolling@1 active (00:01:05, 00:00:42 and 00:10:00), as on the 1.x line.
  FromExecutePipelineCommand@1 stays in the definitions, commented out. Nothing else ever
  started them: a tenant had to be edited by hand before it received anything, and a
  blueprint update reverted that edit. Per trigger the adapter skips a tick while the
  previous run is still going, so the 42-second poll cannot stack runs of the ingest.
Pipeline definitions only. An update takes effect with the next DeployDataFlow of the
DataFlows concerned; on a tenant whose receive-eda-messages DataFlow is deployed, that
deploy starts the polling.

2.6.0 -> 2.7.0: request-consumption-reports and request-missing-consumption-reports work
again (AB#4551). Both were installed as no-ops, because the 1.x line found its days in the
daily EnergyQuantity entities and the stream data had no counterpart yet.
- What counts is what counted on the 1.x line: its daily quantity was built from the
  registers 1-1:2.9.0 G.03 (consumer) and 1-1:2.9.0 G.01T with 1-1:2.9.0 P.01T (producer),
  with the worst quality of the day. Both pipelines look at the measurement anchors of
  these registers only; an L3 value in another register never led to a request.
- request-consumption-reports reads the days whose worst quality is L3 from the daily
  rollup (dataquality_max = 3), oldest day first, at most 800 rows per run (the cap of the
  largest 1.x tenant; the 1.x seed said 400). The cut-off is midnight UTC of today minus
  consumptionRecordRequestDelay days, whatever the time zone of the adapter host; the
  newest day requested is the Vienna day of that date, as on the 1.x line. Only anchors
  that belong to a metering point are read, so a leftover anchor cannot use up the row
  limit. One CR_REQ_PT per metering point and day; the row window of the rollup is the
  calendar day (Europe/Vienna) and becomes the range of the request. A day that also
  holds a manual entry is not requested — its worst quality is not L3.
- The cron trigger `request-low-quality-data` (`0 0 5 * * *`) is part of the seed and the
  pipeline starts on FromPipelineTriggerEvent@1. The 1.x tenants had created this trigger
  by hand; it was never in the deployment repository.
- request-missing-consumption-reports (POST /requestMissingConsumptionReports, body `date`)
  counts the rows of the day in the raw archive and requests every participating metering
  point without a single one. A day with values missing in between counts as present, as
  on the 1.x line.
Needs no newer adapter than 2.5.0 already asks for: GetStreamData@1 (Mesh Adapter SDK
r3.4.85) and AggregateStreamData@1 (r3.4.89) are older than SaveTimeRangeSeriesInArchive@1,
so an EDA adapter from r3.4.141 on carries all three. An adapter version is not expressible
as a blueprint dependency; an older adapter fails the two pipelines with an unknown node
type.
An update takes effect with the next DeployDataFlow of the two DataFlows; that of
request-consumption-reports (692448a0911382c3502c6b95) also deploys the new cron trigger,
and from then on requests go to the grid operators every morning. After an interruption
of reception, deploy it only once reception runs again and the values delivered in the
meantime are ingested, otherwise the days of the interruption are requested although
their better values are already waiting. Nothing calls
request-missing-consumption-reports by itself.
